segments.say: Lesson 19. Design a Notification System. Multi-channel (push, S M S, email, in-app), preferences, templates, priorities, retries and dedupe.

Design a system that sends notifications through push, S M S, email and in-app channels: respecting user preferences, prioritising urgent messages, retrying failures and never double-sending. Here is an analogy. A post office sorting room: urgent letters go in the express bin, bulk mail in another, every letter is logged, and failed deliveries are retried or returned.

Why does this matter? A common design question that exercises queues, retries, idempotency and third-party providers. A few key words. Channel: Push, S M S, email, in-app. Provider: External sender like A P Ns, F C M, Twilio, S E S. Priority queue: Urgent messages processed first. Deduplication: Never send the same notification twice.
Notification pipeline. Any service calls one Notification A P I with (user, type, data, idempotency key). No service talks to Twilio or A P Ns directly.
Check user preferences (channel opt-outs, quiet hours, language) and frequency caps, then render the template.
Enqueue by priority: an O T P must not wait behind 10M marketing emails. Separate queues or topics per priority and channel.
Channel workers call providers (A P Ns, F C M, Twilio, S E S) with rate limits per provider, retries with backoff, and failover to a second provider.
Record every attempt in a delivery log: dedupe by idempotency key, track status (sent, delivered, opened), drive retries and analytics.

Key design points. At-least-once delivery from queues plus dedupe by notification I D, so users don't get the same O T P twice. Priority isolation, per-provider rate limiting and circuit breakers. Templates with localization. Batching into digests for low-priority messages. Device token management (invalid tokens from A P Ns/F C M get cleaned up). Scheduling (send at 9 am local) via a delayed queue or scheduler.

Say it in the interview. "A central notification service validates requests with idempotency keys, applies preferences, quiet hours and caps, renders templates, and enqueues into priority-separated queues per channel. Workers send via providers with rate limiting, retries and failover, while a delivery log handles dedupe, status tracking and analytics.".

Let's compare. Push (A P Ns/F C M): seconds, ~free, engagement, alerts. S M S: seconds, $$ per msg, O T P, critical. Email: seconds–minutes, cheap, receipts, digests. In-app: real-time when open, free, activity feed.

A likely interview question: Design a notification system. A strong answer: Central A P I with idempotency, preferences, caps and templates, priority queues per channel, workers with provider rate limits, retries and failover, delivery log for dedupe and status, scheduling and analytics.
That's it for Design a Notification System. Now play the quiz and games in the app to lock it in. See you in the next lesson.
